clue.text: Bishop travels amid confusion who looks after the train?

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
rides means travels, as on horseback

indicators.note: in confusion means the word just before it is jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A bishop moves through a muddle, and someone asks who is minding the railway train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusion' scrambles AMID into MAID. The definition plays on a wedding dress's train, not a railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's attendant carries or arranges the long trailing part of her wedding gown.

clue.text: A loser, given drug by people?

parts.note: a race is a people or ethnic group
horse is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Someone who failed was handed narcotics by a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given ... by' sets the drug beside the people. The definition is cryptic: a thoroughbred that runs and loses.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner in a race may well finish unplaced, so a loser is one example of the animal, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Capital husband invested in food store

indicators.note: invested in means the husband's letter is placed inside the shop's word

parts.note: a deli (delicatessen) is a shop selling prepared foods

explanation.surface: A husband has put money into a grocery business.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian capital city, the national seat of government in its New form.

clue.text: Bar, say, used by junior member of crew

annotationWithheld.why: Bar, say, used by junior member of crew (5-4): SPEAK (say) is clear, but no sound reading makes 'used by junior member of crew' give EASY, and no blog or database gives the parse
annotationWithheld.clue: Bar, say, used by junior member of crew

clue.text: Dreadful answer by minor incomplete

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: incomplete means the word for minor loses its last letter

parts.note: small means minor or slight

explanation.surface: A response from a child that was unfinished was terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean extremely bad, as in very poor weather or an appalling performance.

clue.text: Composer best known for magical pupil

definitions.text: Composer best known for magical pupil

parts.words: Composer best known for magical pupil
parts.note: the magical pupil is the Sorcerer's Apprentice, the French composer's famous orchestral scherzo, later used in Disney's Fantasia

explanation.surface: A musician whose fame rests on one piece about an enchanted student.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul, the French composer, wrote L'Apprenti sorcier in 1897, his one widely known work.

clue.text: Author of non-U book of instruction

indicators.note: non-U means without U, so the letter U is removed from the word for the book

parts.note: a guide is a handbook or manual of instruction

explanation.surface: A writer of a manual not considered upper-class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-U' is also the British term for vocabulary not used by the upper class, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: André, the French novelist and Nobel laureate who wrote The Immoralist.

clue.text: Way in which Conservative succeeds with risky way to infiltrate party

indicators.note: succeeds means the Conservative's letter follows the way in

parts.note: a gate is an entrance, a way in
rash means reckless or risky

explanation.surface: A Tory triumphs by reckless means of getting into a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' looks political but is a social gathering; 'with' is only a link, and 'succeeds' puts the Conservative after the way in.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn up uninvited at a social event is the method of getting in without a ticket or invitation.

clue.text: Concise reference work covering a lot of maxims

indicators.note: in a down answer, covering means sitting on top of the next piece

parts.note: dict. is the short form of dictionary, a reference work, made concise by abbreviation

explanation.surface: A short encyclopaedia includes many sayings.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the Latin word for a saying, so several authoritative pronouncements or sayings.

clue.text: Person rowing at stern of dinghy has little room to work in

parts.note: a sculler propels a boat with a pair of oars

indicators.note: the stern is the back of a boat, so this takes the last letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: An oarsman at the back of a small boat has scarcely any space to operate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little room' reads as cramped space but defines a small back-kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A small back room for washing dishes and other kitchen chores.

clue.text: Tawdry stuff to equip school

parts.note: to kit out is to equip

explanation.surface: Cheap tat bought to fit out a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaudy objects in poor taste, often valued ironically.

clue.text: Psychiatrist's contract

definitions.meaning: slang for a psychiatrist, short for head-shrinker
to contract is to get smaller

explanation.surface: A therapist's employment agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is a link ('is'); 'contract' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal name for a mental-health doctor; also the verb for becoming smaller.

clue.text: One may extemporise, but not without notes

definitions.text: One may extemporise, but not without notes

parts.words: One may extemporise, but not without notes
parts.note: extemporising suggests speaking without notes, but a player who improvises still needs musical notes

explanation.surface: A speaker may ad-lib, yet still keeps prompts.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer of music may improvise, and still uses musical notes.

clue.text: Alternatives at roulette one briefly generated

indicators.note: one of them shortened means just the initial letter of the first colour is kept

parts.note: the colour bets at roulette are black and red
the other roulette colour is red

explanation.surface: A gambler's choice of colours, one quickly made.
explanation.walkthrough: The two roulette colours are BLACK and RED; 'one briefly' cuts BLACK to B.
explanation.definitionFit: Generated and produced, as animals reared or brought into being.

clue.text: Competition for all-rounders he can't hold candle to, doubly indisposed

annotationWithheld.why: Competition for all-rounders he can't hold candle to, doubly indisposed (9): the letters of 'he can't hold' give DECATHLON plus a spare H, and 'candle to' needs an H from nowhere; no reading of 'doubly indisposed' resolves it, and no source gives the parse
annotationWithheld.clue: Competition for all-rounders he can't hold candle to, doubly indisposed

clue.text: Identifies island going West without a sailor

indicators.note: without means outside, so the reversed run goes round the A
in an across answer, going West means the run of letters so far is read right to left

parts.note: to name is to identify
Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone names an island heading west without a seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going West' turns NAMES plus ELBA into ABLESEMAN; 'without a' then puts that run outside an A. 'sailor' is the definition, not Napoleon on Elba.
explanation.definitionFit: A rating in the Royal Navy above ordinary seaman, a qualified deckhand.

clue.text: Indirect illumination is hoisted over entrance

indicators.note: in a down answer, over means placed above the next piece
in a down answer, hoisted means lifted so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
to entrance (en-TRANCE) is to delight or enchant

explanation.surface: A lamp is raised above a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' looks like a doorway but is the verb meaning enchant. 'hoisted' turns IS into SI.
explanation.definitionFit: Light from the side, or figuratively incidental information shed on a subject.

clue.text: A time to include US players in humiliation

indicators.note: to include means the A and T go around the players

parts.note: taken as written
basemen are fielders in American baseball

explanation.surface: A period that takes in American athletes ends in disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: BASEMEN fits between the A and the T.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of being degraded or brought low, a loss of dignity.

clue.text: Where invaders land around unknown point on our coast

indicators.note: around means the invaders' landing place goes about the unknown

parts.note: a beachhead is the shoreline position an invading force first seizes
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Invaders come ashore near some unidentified spot on the British shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like 'near' but means the landing word wraps the Y. BEACHY HEAD is a chalk headland on the Sussex coast of southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A headland or promontory on the English Channel near Eastbourne, a point being a projecting piece of coast.

clue.text: Artist of classical type in Spain

definitions.meaning: a painter, Domenikos Theotokopoulos of Toledo
the painter's Spanish nickname means the Greek, a person of the classical nationality

explanation.surface: A painter in the classical manner working in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading translates: a classical type is a Greek, and 'in Spain' asks for it in Spanish, with the article.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cretan-born painter worked in Spain, where his nickname means 'the Greek'.

clue.text: Swindle American feller with house

parts.note: ax is the American spelling of axe, a tool for felling trees

explanation.surface: A con involving a US lumberjack and a property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feller' looks like 'fellow' but means a thing that fells. 'with' sets the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A deceptive trick or fraud meant to fool people.

clue.text: Namely, an article that's caustic

parts.note: sc. (scilicet) is the abbreviation for namely
an gives A
a thing is an article or object

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry names a piece of writing that is bitingly critical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' suggests a grammatical article or a newspaper piece but means an object.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe bitterly severe criticism that wounds.

clue.text: Trumpet improvisation contributing to music on channel

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A trumpeter's ad-lib adds to a broadcast's music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'improvisation' suggests a jazz solo, but it means a makeshift instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A large spiral seashell blown as a makeshift horn, an improvised trumpet.

clue.text: Disguised one new person of little importance

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a cog is a minor part in a big machine

explanation.surface: Someone unrecognisable is a newcomer of low status.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for incognito, concealing one's true identity.

clue.text: It divides Irish citizens, left uncertain about English

indicators.note: about means the word for uncertain goes around the English letter

parts.note: iffy means doubtful or uncertain

explanation.surface: Something splits the Irish people, leaving them doubtful about England.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests politics, but the citizens are Dubliners, and the divider a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The river running through Dublin separates its northside and southside residents.

clue.text: Rifle shot makes one jump

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or broken, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gun going off startles someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes one jump' looks like the effect of a gunshot, but 'makes' is a link and 'one jump' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A flying leap, a bound taken at speed.

clue.text: In a mass written by Messiaen or Berlioz

definitions.text: In a mass written by Messiaen or Berlioz

parts.words: In a mass written by Messiaen or Berlioz
parts.note: a Mass by either French composer suggests church music, but the reading is French words meaning all together

explanation.surface: A Catholic Mass setting by one of two French composers.
explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase meaning all together as a whole, as a Frenchman would write it.

clue.text: Times crossword? Most would find the result hard to swallow

definitions.text: Times crossword? Most would find the result hard to swallow

parts.words: Times crossword? Most would find the result hard to swallow
parts.note: the device times a boil, and leaving it too long gives a hard-boiled result

explanation.surface: Solvers find the newspaper's puzzle tough going.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sand-glass timing boiled breakfast eggs; overcook and they come out hard.

clue.text: It may be said to limit one's drinking supply

definitions.text: It may be said to limit one's drinking supply

parts.words: It may be said to limit one's drinking supply
parts.note: a host pouring a drink asks a guest to say the word to stop at the right amount

explanation.surface: A phrase that rations a drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: The word in 'say when', the guest's cue to stop pouring.

clue.text: Lay down life for another?

parts.note: sounds like self-sacrifice, but means setting down a life story on paper on someone else's behalf

explanation.surface: Sacrificing oneself for someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: To write a book, often a memoir, credited to someone else.
